answer: Sequential Proof-of-Latency Windows. Each identity must answer a random challenge within a tight time window; the challenge seed derives from a comet observation timestamp published after the window opens. Answers are checked against a cipher commitment, and each identity's response pattern is mapped into a nebula of historical timing data. Attackers paying per-identity compute cannot parallelize responses without violating latency bounds, so each fake identity costs dedicated hardware and an idle waiting period, not just capital.
